max.description: Maximum detectable distance (farthest valid return). Unit: "m". Maps to SDF lidar/range/max.

resolution.description: Radial distance resolution: smallest resolvable change in measured distance along a beam. Unit: "m". Maps to SDF lidar/range/resolution. Distinct from the per-axis angular resolution in scan-pattern.

range.description: Distance measurement range of the ranging sensor: minimum and maximum detectable distance and the radial (range) resolution. Maps losslessly to SDF lidar/<range> (min/max/resolution). Distinct from the angular scan-pattern (which describes sweep angles): this is the along-beam distance the sensor can report.

scan-pattern.description: Per-axis angular scan pattern (samples/resolution/min-angle/max-angle for the horizontal and vertical axes), the lossless target for a converted URDF ray/LaserRay sensor. Optional; complements the aggregate channels/fov fields above.

noise.description: Range/beam noise model for the lidar (SDF lidar/ray <noise>). Applies to the measured distance along each beam. Optional; absent => ideal (noiseless) ranging.

lidar_params.description: Lidar-specific parameters defining scan geometry, point cloud density, and environmental robustness. Applies to optical sensors with type="lidar".

samples.description: Number of samples (beams) along this axis. URDF ray horizontal/vertical @samples.

resolution.description: Angular resolution multiplier along this axis. URDF ray @resolution.

min-angle.description: Minimum sweep angle in radians. URDF ray @min_angle.

max-angle.description: Maximum sweep angle in radians. URDF ray @max_angle.

lidar_scan_axis.description: One axis of a lidar/ray angular scan pattern, matching a URDF ray <horizontal>/<vertical> element (samples, angular resolution, and min/max sweep angle). This is the lossless target for a converted URDF ray sensor; it complements the aggregate fields (channels, fov) which describe the device rather than the per-axis sampling.

range.description: Maximum range of the light in meters: beyond this the light contributes nothing. SDF light/attenuation/range.

linear.description: Linear attenuation factor (0-1): 1 attenuates evenly over the range. SDF light/attenuation/linear.

constant.description: Constant attenuation factor: 1.0 never attenuates, 0.0 is complete attenuation. SDF light/attenuation/constant.

quadratic.description: Quadratic attenuation factor: adds curvature to the falloff. SDF light/attenuation/quadratic.

light_attenuation.description: Distance attenuation of a scene-illumination light: how its intensity falls off with range. Maps to SDF light/attenuation. The effective factor at distance d is 1/(constant + linear*d + quadratic*d^2), clamped to zero beyond range.

predecessor.description: Predecessor body (comp name) in the kinematic loop at this closure point.

successor.description: Successor body (comp name) in the kinematic loop at this closure point.

constraint-axes.description: 6-value string "tx ty tz rx ry rz" where 1=constrained, 0=free. Example: "1 1 1 1 1 0" constrains all except rotation around Z.

loop_closure.description: Marks a joint as closing a kinematic loop. Contains the predecessor/successor bodies and which DOFs are constrained at the closure point. Used by dynamics solvers (HyRoDyn, Drake) to handle parallel mechanisms that URDF's tree-only structure cannot represent.

unit.description: Physical unit of the measurement. Optional; if omitted, the SI default for the parent element applies. Specify explicitly for non-SI units (e.g., "RPM/V", "deg", "rpm", "g", "dps", "mK") or when the unit is ambiguous.

measured_value.description: A scalar measurement with an optional unit. The text content is the numeric value. HCDF assumes SI units by default: if the unit attribute is omitted, the parent element's documented default SI unit applies (meters for length, kg for mass, radians for angles, seconds for time, Hz for frequency, V for voltage, A for current, W for power, ohm for resistance, Nm for torque, N for force, degC for temperature, Mbps for network speed). Specify unit explicitly only when using a non-SI unit or when the context is ambiguous (e.g., velocity-constant where unit distinguishes Ke from Kv). Example: <speed>100</speed> means 100 Mbps (SI default for speed). <velocity-constant unit="RPM/V">920</velocity-constant> needs explicit unit.

submesh.description: Optional selection of a single named sub-part within the mesh file (SDF mesh/submesh). Absent => load the whole file.

uri.description: URI of the mesh file (relative to the HCDF document or absolute). Required.

scale.description: Scale factors as three space-separated doubles "sx sy sz" applied to the mesh. Default: "1 1 1" (no scaling).

sha.description: SHA-256 hash of the mesh file for content integrity and content-addressed caching. Optional but recommended for reproducible builds. Mirrors model_ref/@sha so primitive mesh refs are integrity-checkable too.

source-uri.description: URI of the original pre-conversion asset (e.g. the STL/DAE/OBJ this mesh was converted from when targeting GLB/glTF). Optional; lets tooling reuse the source for a higher-fidelity reverse conversion.

mesh.description: External 3D mesh geometry loaded from a file. Supports GLB, glTF, STL, OBJ, and DAE formats.

joint.description: Name of the leader joint to mimic. Required. Semantic rule: must reference an existing joint defined in the HCDF document.

multiplier.description: Scaling factor applied to the leader joint's position. Default: 1.0 (identical motion). Use -1 for opposite-direction coupling.

offset.description: Constant offset added after scaling (radians for revolute, meters for prismatic). Default: 0.

mimic.description: Mimic joint constraint. Makes this joint's position track another joint's position via a linear relationship: position = multiplier * leader_position + offset. Used for mechanically coupled joints (e.g., parallel gripper fingers, coupled four-bar linkages).

items.description: Include-mode selector: draw this named node subtree; repeated, the UNION of several. Reuses the <submesh> type (name + optional @center). The subtree keeps its model-root-relative transform (no recenter). @center is honored only when this is the LONE selector on the <model> (one <submesh>, no siblings, no exclusions); the validator rejects @center on a union member. MUST NOT be combined with <exclude-submesh>; mixing include and exclude is a validator error.

submesh.description: Include-mode selector: draw this named node subtree; repeated, the UNION of several. Reuses the <submesh> type (name + optional @center). The subtree keeps its model-root-relative transform (no recenter). @center is honored only when this is the LONE selector on the <model> (one <submesh>, no siblings, no exclusions); the validator rejects @center on a union member. MUST NOT be combined with <exclude-submesh>; mixing include and exclude is a validator error.

items.description: Exclude-mode selector: draw the whole model MINUS this named node subtree; repeated, minus all of them. The complement of <submesh>; the dedicated type carries no @center (a subtraction has nothing to recenter). MUST NOT be combined with <submesh>; mixing exclude and include is a validator error. Motivating case: a shared actuator GLB whose case visual is the whole model excluding the flange subtree (case, connectors, and pin anchors come along implicitly as the CAD grows), paired with a flange visual on the sibling comp that is the matching <submesh> include.

exclude-submesh.description: Exclude-mode selector: draw the whole model MINUS this named node subtree; repeated, minus all of them. The complement of <submesh>; the dedicated type carries no @center (a subtraction has nothing to recenter). MUST NOT be combined with <submesh>; mixing exclude and include is a validator error. Motivating case: a shared actuator GLB whose case visual is the whole model excluding the flange subtree (case, connectors, and pin anchors come along implicitly as the CAD grows), paired with a flange visual on the sibling comp that is the matching <submesh> include.

uri.description: URI of the 3D model file (GLB/glTF format). Relative to the HCDF document or absolute. Required.

sha.description: SHA-256 hash of the referenced file for content integrity verification. Optional but recommended for reproducible builds.

model_ref.description: Reference to an external 3D model file (GLB or glTF) for high-fidelity visual representation. Preferred over geometry primitives when available. Optional submesh selectors choose WHICH subtrees of the model this visual draws, in one of three mutually exclusive modes: no selector children draws the WHOLE model (backward compatible; existing docs are unaffected); one or more <submesh> draws the UNION of the named node subtrees (include mode); one or more <exclude-submesh> draws the whole model MINUS the named subtrees (exclude mode). MIXING <submesh> with <exclude-submesh> on one <model> is an ERROR: the modes are exclusive, but the grammar cannot forbid the pair cleanly (both are optional repeated children), so the companion validator rejects the mix rather than the XSD. Selected subtrees KEEP their model-root-relative node transforms (geometry is NOT recentered), so parts split out of one shared GLB keep their authored relative placement. @center on a <submesh> is honored ONLY on a LONE include (a single <submesh>, no siblings, no exclusions) and the validator rejects it on a union member. Two-comps-one-GLB pattern: to split one sha-addressed GLB across two comps joined by a joint, the parent comp includes one subtree and the child comp the complementary subtree of the SAME GLB, and the child visual's <pose> re-expresses that geometry in the child's comp-local frame (the inverse of the joint origin) so the halves still register.

pose.description: Pose of the motor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

voltage.description: Motor voltage ratings with nominal/continuous/peak/max levels. Unit: typically "V".

current.description: Motor current ratings with nominal/continuous/peak/max levels. Unit: typically "A".

inductance.description: Phase (winding) inductance. Unit: typically "H" (henries) or "mH". A standard BLDC datasheet parameter alongside resistance; the L/R electrical time constant sets the current-loop bandwidth for field-oriented control.

torque-constant.description: Motor torque constant (Kt). Torque output per ampere of current. Unit: typically "Nm/A".

velocity-constant.description: Motor velocity constant: the proportionality between voltage and rotational speed. This single element covers both Ke (back-EMF constant) and Kv (speed constant) conventions; the unit attribute determines which: use unit="V/RPM" or unit="V.s/rad" for Ke (back-EMF style, common on industrial servo and hub motor datasheets, e.g., 0.109 V/RPM for ZLLG65ASM250-L); use unit="RPM/V" for Kv (speed constant style, common on drone/RC BLDC datasheets, e.g., 920 RPM/V). Ke and Kv are reciprocals of each other; an agent computes one from the other as needed.

rotor-inertia.description: Rotor moment of inertia (J) about the motor's rotation axis. Unit: typically "kg.m^2" or "g.cm^2". The rotor's own inertia reflected through a transmission dominates the effective inertia at the joint (reflected_inertia = rotor_inertia x reduction^2), so it is required for the reflected-inertia and acceleration math on quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators.

max-speed.description: Maximum no-load shaft speed. Unit: typically "rpm" or "rad/s".

stall-torque.description: Stall torque at rated voltage. Unit: typically "Nm".

thermal-resistance.description: Thermal resistance from winding to ambient. Unit: typically "degC/W". Used for thermal derating calculations.

max-temperature.description: Maximum allowable winding temperature before demagnetization or insulation failure. Unit: typically "degC".

thrust-axis.description: Direction of thrust force as "x y z" unit vector relative to the component frame. Only for type="thrust". Example: "0 0 1" for upward thrust.

max-thrust.description: Maximum thrust force output. Unit: "N". Only for type="thrust".

pole-pairs.description: Number of magnetic pole pairs in the motor. Determines the electrical frequency: electrical_freq = mechanical_rpm × pole_pairs / 60. Critical for BLDC commutation (Hall sensor transitions per revolution = pole_pairs × 6), ESC configuration, and back-EMF frequency. Example: 15 pole pairs for ZLLG65ASM250-L hub motor, 7 for typical drone motor, 2 for industrial servo.

displacement.description: Engine displacement for internal combustion motors. Unit: "cc" (cubic centimeters) or "L" (liters). Only applicable for type="ice". Example: 50cc for a small generator, 0.8L for a robot mower engine.

cylinders.description: Number of cylinders for internal combustion motors. Only applicable for type="ice".

stroke.description: Linear travel range for linear actuators. Unit: "m" or "mm". Defines the maximum extension distance. Only applicable for type="linear".

control-modes.description: Supported control interfaces for this motor.

no-load-speed.description: No-load shaft speed at rated voltage. Unit: "rpm". From motor load test. Higher than rated speed. Example: 257.9 rpm for ZLLG65ASM250-L at 24V.

no-load-current.description: No-load current draw at rated voltage. Unit: "A". The minimum current the motor draws when spinning freely. Important for idle power budget. Example: 0.974A.

max-power-out.description: Maximum mechanical power output from load test. Unit: "W". The peak of the power-vs-torque curve. Example: 158.8W at 11.61 Nm for ZLLG65ASM250-L.

max-efficiency.description: Peak efficiency from load test. Unit: "percent". The best-case power_out/power_in ratio. Example: 68.4% at 3.84 Nm / 216.3 RPM. An agent should target this operating point for best runtime.

name.description: Unique name for this motor within the component (e.g., "shoulder_motor", "wheel_fl"). Required. Referenced by transmission elements.

type.description: Motor technology type (bldc, brushed, stepper, servo, linear, hydraulic, pneumatic, thrust, ice). Optional; useful for selecting appropriate control algorithms.

construction.description: Motor physical construction: "inrunner" (rotor inside stator, higher RPM, common in industrial servos and drone motors), "outrunner" (rotor outside stator, higher torque, common in hub motors and large drone motors), "axial-flux" (flat pancake design, very thin, high torque density), "pancake" (flat form factor). Only relevant for BLDC/brushed motors.

visual.description: Name of the visual element containing this motor's mesh for 3D highlighting.

mesh.description: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this motor.

encoder.description: Name reference to an encoder sensor on this component. Identifies motor-side position feedback. The encoder is a full sensor with its own pose, driver, noise model, and resolution.

hall.description: Name reference to a Hall sensor on this component used for BLDC commutation. Typically an em-type sensor with 3 Hall elements (U/V/W) providing 6-step commutation signals. Often shares the motor signal connector with the encoder.

thermistor.description: Name reference to a temperature sensor on this component monitoring motor winding temperature. Typically an NTC thermistor embedded in the motor stator. Used for thermal protection: the agent can monitor temperature and derate or shut down before exceeding max-temperature.

motor.description: Motor or actuator with electrical, mechanical, and thermal parameters. Voltage and current use rated_value type with nominal/continuous/peak/max ratings. Connected to joints via transmission elements.

mean.description: Mean of the noise distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

stddev.description: Standard deviation of the noise distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

bias-mean.description: Mean of the static bias distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

bias-stddev.description: Standard deviation of the static bias distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

precision.description: Quantization precision (ADC resolution). Output is rounded to the nearest multiple of this value. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

dynamic-bias-stddev.description: Standard deviation of the DYNAMIC bias process: a slowly time-varying bias (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck / first-order Gauss-Markov), distinct from the static bias random walk (bias-mean/bias-stddev). Maps to SDF noise/dynamic_bias_stddev. Default: 0 (no dynamic bias). Units match the sensor's measurement unit.

dynamic-bias-correlation-time.description: Correlation time (in seconds) of the dynamic bias process: the time constant over which the dynamic bias decorrelates. Maps to SDF noise/dynamic_bias_correlation_time. Larger values = slower drift. Only meaningful when dynamic-bias-stddev is set.

type.description: Noise distribution type. Required. Use "gaussian" for realistic sensor simulation, "none" for ideal sensors.

noise.description: Sensor noise model for simulation. Specifies the statistical distribution and parameters applied to ideal sensor readings. For gaussian type: output = ideal + N(mean, stddev) + bias where bias ~ N(bias-mean, bias-stddev). For uniform type: output = ideal + U(mean - stddev, mean + stddev).

pose.description: Pose of the optical sensor module relative to the sensor group origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

driver.description: Driver identification for the optical sensor (e.g., "oak-d-pro", "rplidar-a2", "vl53l5cx").

geometry.description: Geometry for visualizing the optical sensor housing.

items.description: Field-of-view definition(s). One per sensing cone/pyramid. Stereo cameras have two FoVs; omnidirectional lidars may have one 360-degree FoV.

fov.description: Field-of-view definition(s). One per sensing cone/pyramid. Stereo cameras have two FoVs; omnidirectional lidars may have one 360-degree FoV.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth for network planning. Cameras and lidars generate significant data; an agent uses this to validate TSN schedules and link capacity.

camera-params.description: Camera-specific parameters (shutter, HDR, compression, trigger, thermal specs). Use when type="camera" or type="thermal".

lidar-params.description: Lidar-specific parameters (scan-type, channels, points-per-second, returns, wavelength). Use when type="lidar".

type.description: Optical sensor sub-type (camera, thermal, lidar, tof, optical_flow). Required.

optical_sensor.description: Optical sensor (camera, lidar, ToF, optical flow). Contains one or more field-of-view definitions, each with its own intrinsics, distortion, and noise model.

xyz.description: Position as three space-separated doubles "x y z" in meters. Default: "0 0 0" (origin of parent frame).

rpy.description: Orientation as three space-separated Euler angles "roll pitch yaw" in radians (XYZ extrinsic convention). Default: "0 0 0" (no rotation).

quat.description: Orientation as quaternion "x y z w" (Hamilton convention, scalar-last), exactly four doubles. Optional; if present, overrides rpy (quat-wins precedence).

pose.description: 6-DOF pose (position + orientation) of an element relative to its parent frame. Specify position via xyz and orientation via either rpy (Euler angles) or quat (quaternion). If both rpy and quat are given, quat takes precedence.

fuel-cell.description: Fuel cell energy converter (PEM, DMFC, SOFC). Generates electricity from fuel continuously.

solar.description: Solar panel energy source. Generates electricity from sunlight via photovoltaic cells.

supercapacitor.description: Supercapacitor for peak power buffering, regenerative braking energy capture, and pulsed load smoothing.

name.description: Unique name for this power source.

role.description: Power source role in the system: "primary" (main power source), "backup" (engaged on primary failure), "hot-swap" (can be replaced while system runs on other source), "ups" (uninterruptible: provides power during switchover). An agent uses this for power redundancy analysis.

group.description: Power source group name for failover pairing. Sources in the same group can substitute for each other. Example: group="main" on two hot-swap batteries means either can power the system alone while the other is replaced.

visual.description: Name of the visual element containing this power source's mesh for 3D highlighting.

mesh.description: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this power source.

power_source.description: Energy source on a component. Contains one or more source types (battery, tank, fuel-cell, solar, supercapacitor). An agent computes runtime, power budget, and weight impact from this data. The component's POWER port defines the electrical output; the power-source defines the stored or generated energy.

pitch.description: Propeller pitch: theoretical distance advanced per revolution in ideal fluid. Unit: "m" or "in".

direction.description: Rotation direction viewed from above/front: "CW" (clockwise) or "CCW" (counter-clockwise). Critical for torque balancing on multirotors.

prop_surface.description: Propeller surface: generates thrust from rotation. Used on multirotors, fixed-wing aircraft, boats, and underwater vehicles. The associated motor provides torque; the propeller converts it to thrust based on diameter, pitch, and blade geometry.

frequency.description: Operating frequency. 77-79GHz = automotive standard (high resolution). 24GHz = industrial (longer range, lower resolution). Unit: "GHz".

modulation.description: Modulation scheme: "fmcw" (Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave, automotive standard, measures range + velocity simultaneously) or "pulsed" (traditional, longer range).

azimuth-fov.description: Horizontal field of view. Unit: "deg". Typical: 120 short-range, 20 long-range.

elevation-fov.description: Vertical field of view (4D imaging radar). Unit: "deg". Presence indicates elevation-capable radar.

azimuth-resolution.description: Azimuth angular resolution: minimum angle to separate two targets horizontally. Unit: "deg".

range-resolution.description: Range resolution: minimum distance to separate two targets at the same angle. Unit: "m". Determined by chirp bandwidth.

velocity-resolution.description: Velocity resolution: minimum speed difference to separate two targets. Unit: "m/s".

max-detections.description: Maximum simultaneous target detections per frame.

mimo.description: MIMO antenna configuration as "NtxMrx" (e.g., "3tx4rx" = 12 virtual channels). More virtual channels = better angular resolution.

radar_params.description: Radar-specific parameters for 4D imaging radar and distance/velocity sensing. Applies to rf sensors with type="radar".

pose.description: Pose of the sensor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

driver.description: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.

noise.description: Noise model for the sensor output.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).

type.description: Radiation sensor type (geiger, scintillation, neutron, dosimeter). Required.

radiation_sensor.description: Radiation sensor for detecting ionizing radiation. Used on nuclear inspection robots, space robots, and environmental monitoring platforms. Extends sensor_base with radiation type attribute.

unit.description: Physical unit. Optional; SI default applies if omitted.

min.description: Minimum acceptable value in the specified unit.

max.description: Maximum acceptable value in the specified unit.

range_value.description: A value with minimum and maximum bounds and an optional unit. The text content is the nominal value. Used for port voltage ranges, temperature operating ranges, and similar bounded quantities. SI defaults apply when unit is omitted (V for voltage, degC for temperature, etc.).

unit.description: Physical unit. Optional; V for voltage elements, A for current elements by SI default.

nominal.description: Nominal (design-point) operating value. The steady-state value the motor is designed for.

continuous.description: Maximum continuous value the motor can sustain indefinitely without overheating.

peak.description: Peak value the motor can sustain for a short duration (typically seconds to minutes) before thermal limits are reached.

max.description: Absolute maximum value. Exceeding this causes permanent damage or triggers hardware protection.

rated_value.description: A value with multiple rating levels for motor electrical parameters. Text content is the primary value. Used for motor voltage (default unit: V) and current (default unit: A) where different operating regimes apply (nominal steady-state, continuous thermal limit, short-term peak, absolute maximum). SI defaults apply when unit is omitted.

driver.description: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.

noise.description: Noise model for the sensor output.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).

radar-params.description: Radar-specific parameters (frequency, modulation, FOV, resolution, velocity, MIMO). Use when type="radar".

gnss-params.description: GNSS-specific parameters (constellations, frequencies, RTK, accuracy, PPS). Use when type="gnss".

type.description: RF sensor sub-type (gnss, uwb, radar, radio_altimeter). Required.

rf_sensor.description: Radio-frequency sensor (GNSS receiver, UWB ranger, radar, radio altimeter). Extends sensor_base with type-specific parameter blocks for radar and GNSS.

safety_controller.description: URDF joint safety_controller (soft-limit controller). Zero cyber-physical meaning; carried for lossless URDF round-trip only. Mirrors urdf.xsd safety_controller (k_velocity required).

items.description: A pair of components to disable collision checking between.

pair.description: A pair of components to disable collision checking between.

self_collision_disable.description: List of component pairs to skip for self-collision checking. Dramatically improves motion planning performance: typically 80%+ of all link pairs can be skipped. Equivalent to SRDF disable_collisions.

items.description: Inertial measurement unit(s): accelerometers and/or gyroscopes.

inertial.description: Inertial measurement unit(s): accelerometers and/or gyroscopes.

items.description: Electromagnetic sensor(s): magnetometers, metal detectors, eddy current probes.

em.description: Electromagnetic sensor(s): magnetometers, metal detectors, eddy current probes.

items.description: Optical sensor(s): cameras, lidars, ToF sensors, optical flow sensors.

optical.description: Optical sensor(s): cameras, lidars, ToF sensors, optical flow sensors.

items.description: Radio-frequency sensor(s): GNSS receivers, UWB rangers, radars, radio altimeters.

rf.description: Radio-frequency sensor(s): GNSS receivers, UWB rangers, radars, radio altimeters.

items.description: Chemical/environmental sensor(s): gas detectors, pH sensors, humidity sensors.

chemical.description: Chemical/environmental sensor(s): gas detectors, pH sensors, humidity sensors.

items.description: Force/torque sensor(s): strain gauges, pressure transducers, torque sensors, load cells.

force.description: Force/torque sensor(s): strain gauges, pressure transducers, torque sensors, load cells.

items.description: Position/velocity encoder(s): motor-side, joint-side, wheel, or linear. Optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, or resistive principle.

encoder.description: Position/velocity encoder(s): motor-side, joint-side, wheel, or linear. Optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, or resistive principle.

items.description: Temperature sensor(s): thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples, IR. Common: motor winding temp, battery cell temp, ambient.

temperature.description: Temperature sensor(s): thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples, IR. Common: motor winding temp, battery cell temp, ambient.

items.description: Radiation sensor(s): Geiger counters, scintillation detectors, neutron sensors, dosimeters.

radiation.description: Radiation sensor(s): Geiger counters, scintillation detectors, neutron sensors, dosimeters.

items.description: Audio/acoustic sensor(s): microphones, ultrasonic transducers, sonar, hydrophones.

audio.description: Audio/acoustic sensor(s): microphones, ultrasonic transducers, sonar, hydrophones.

items.description: Tactile/contact sensor(s): capacitive arrays, FSR pads, piezoelectric skins, barometric patches, optical gel sensors. Provides spatially distributed pressure/contact data for grasp planning, slip detection, and safe interaction.

tactile.description: Tactile/contact sensor(s): capacitive arrays, FSR pads, piezoelectric skins, barometric patches, optical gel sensors. Provides spatially distributed pressure/contact data for grasp planning, slip detection, and safe interaction.

items.description: Fluid sensor(s): barometers, airspeed/pitot sensors, depth sensors, flow meters, liquid-level sensors, and general pressure transducers. Measurand is gas/liquid pressure or flow (distinct from force = solid contact and chemical = composition).

fluid.description: Fluid sensor(s): barometers, airspeed/pitot sensors, depth sensors, flow meters, liquid-level sensors, and general pressure transducers. Measurand is gas/liquid pressure or flow (distinct from force = solid contact and chemical = composition).

name.description: Unique name for this sensor group within the component (e.g., "imu_main", "front_camera_suite"). Required.

update-rate.description: Sensor output update rate in Hz. Applies to all sub-sensors in this group unless overridden. Optional.

sensor.description: Sensor hardware container grouped by physical measurement category. Contains sub-elements for inertial (accel, gyro), electromagnetic (mag), optical (camera, lidar, tof, optical flow), RF (gnss, uwb, radar), chemical (gas, ph, humidity), force (strain, pressure, torque, load cell), encoder (position/velocity feedback), temperature (thermistor, RTD, thermocouple, IR), radiation (geiger, scintillation, neutron, dosimeter), audio (microphone, ultrasonic, sonar, hydrophone), tactile (capacitive, resistive, piezoelectric, barometric, optical), and fluid (barometer, airspeed, depth, flow, level, differential, gauge, absolute, sealed, vacuum) sensors. Each sub-sensor has pose, driver identification, measurement parameters, and noise model.

pose.description: Pose of the sensor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

driver.description: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.

noise.description: Noise model for the sensor output.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).

sensor_base.description: Base sensor type with elements common to ALL sensor subtypes: pose, driver, range, resolution, noise, data output, and geometry. Extended by em, rf, chemical, force, and encoder sensor types. ODR/bandwidth/FIFO are NOT included here; those are specific to high-rate inertial sensors and live in sensor_params (accel/gyro blocks).

axis-align.description: Axis remapping from sensor internal axes to component body frame. Optional; omit if sensor axes match body frame.

name.description: Driver identifier string used by the runtime to load the correct sensor driver (e.g., "bmi088", "icm42688p", "bmp390"). Required.

sensor_driver.description: Sensor driver identification and configuration. Maps the physical sensor to a software driver by name and provides axis alignment correction for the driver's coordinate frame.

description.description: Human-readable description of this FoV (e.g., "left stereo camera", "forward-facing depth").

pose.description: Pose of the FoV origin relative to the sensor origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians). For stereo cameras, this encodes the baseline offset.

geometry.description: FoV volume geometry for visualization. Typically a frustum (conical or pyramidal).

intrinsics.description: Design-spec camera intrinsic parameters (focal length, principal point, image size) from the datasheet. For calibrated values, use the calibration element instead.

distortion.description: Design-spec lens distortion coefficients (Brown-Conrady model). For calibrated values, use the calibration element instead.

lens.description: Lens projection model (fisheye/wide-angle mapping function and field cutoff). Present for non-rectilinear lenses that Brown-Conrady distortion cannot describe; absent => pinhole/rectilinear projection per the intrinsics.

calibration.description: Measured calibration results for this specific camera unit. Contains calibrated intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy), distortion coefficients (k1-k3, p1-p2), reprojection error, calibration date, temperature, and method. When present, agents should use these values instead of the design-spec intrinsics/distortion.

noise.description: Per-pixel noise model for this FoV (e.g., depth noise for ToF sensors).

camera-matrix.description: Full ROS CameraInfo geometry for this FoV beyond the K matrix (intrinsics) and D coefficients (distortion): the rectification matrix R, projection matrix P, pixel binning, and region of interest. Present for a stereo-rectified or cropped/binned camera. Absent => identity rectification, P = K, no binning, full frame.

name.description: Unique name for this FoV within the sensor (e.g., "left", "right", "depth", "rgb"). Required.

color.description: Visualization color for the FoV cone in the 3D viewer (e.g., "0.2 0.8 0.2 0.3" for translucent green RGBA).

sensor_fov.description: Field-of-view definition for an optical sensor. Each FoV represents a distinct sensing cone/pyramid (e.g., a stereo camera has two FoVs). Contains the FoV geometry, design-spec intrinsics, distortion model, calibration results, and noise parameters. The intrinsics/distortion elements hold nominal datasheet values; the calibration element holds measured values from an actual calibration on this specific unit. If calibration is present, agents should use it over the design specs.

range.description: Full-scale measurement range (e.g., 16 with unit="g" for +/-16g accelerometer, 2000 with unit="dps" for gyroscope).

resolution.description: Measurement resolution: smallest detectable change (e.g., 0.488 with unit="mg" for 16-bit at 16g range).

odr.description: Output Data Rate: hardware sampling frequency in Hz. This is how fast the ADC converts, regardless of how often software processes the data. Example: 3200 with unit="Hz". Determines Nyquist frequency (odr/2) and aliasing behavior.

bandwidth.description: Anti-aliasing low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz. Determines the useful signal bandwidth. Typically at or below ODR/2 (Nyquist). Example: 1600 with unit="Hz" for ODR=3200Hz. Lower bandwidth reduces noise but limits frequency response.

fifo.description: Hardware FIFO buffer configuration. When present, the sensor collects samples at ODR rate into a buffer and interrupts at ODR/watermark rate. Example: ODR=3200Hz, fifo watermark=8 → 400Hz interrupt rate delivering 8 samples per burst.

noise.description: Noise model for this measurement axis. Includes measurement-distribution standard deviation, static and dynamic bias terms, and quantization precision. Scalar (isotropic): applies to all three physical axes. For anisotropic per-axis noise, use axis-noise below (this scalar is the fallback).

axis-noise.description: Optional per-axis noise (x/y/z), each a full <noise> model. Present when the accelerometer/gyroscope specifies different noise on each axis (SDF gz-sim per-axis <angular_velocity>/<linear_acceleration> <x|y|z>/<noise> blocks). Complements the scalar <noise> above, which remains the isotropic fallback.

sensor_params.description: Measurement parameters for a sensor axis or channel. Defines the operating range, resolution, sampling rate (ODR), anti-aliasing filter bandwidth, FIFO configuration, and noise model. ODR and bandwidth are distinct: ODR is the hardware sampling rate, bandwidth is the LPF cutoff frequency. The effective processing rate depends on ODR and FIFO watermark.

version.description: Firmware or software version string (e.g., "1.2.3", "v2024.03-rc1"). Semantic versioning recommended.

hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the firmware binary for integrity verification and update tracking.

firmware-manifest-uri.description: URI of the firmware manifest file describing the full firmware package contents, dependencies, and update instructions.

params.description: Runtime configuration parameters string passed to the firmware at boot (e.g., DTS overlay name, boot arguments).

name.description: Firmware or software package name (e.g., "zephyr-flight-controller", "linux-jetson-orin"). Required.

software.description: Firmware or software identity for a component. Used for firmware manifest tracking, version management, and over-the-air update planning.

cell-type.description: Photovoltaic cell technology: "monocrystalline" (highest efficiency 20-24%, rigid panels), "polycrystalline" (lower cost, 15-20% efficiency), "thin-film" (flexible, lightweight, 10-15% efficiency, can conform to curved surfaces), "gaas" (gallium arsenide, 28-30% efficiency, used in space, expensive), "perovskite" (emerging, potentially low cost). Determines efficiency, weight, flexibility, and cost tradeoffs.

peak-power.description: Peak power output under Standard Test Conditions (STC: 1000 W/m2 irradiance, 25 degC cell temperature, AM1.5 spectrum). Unit: "W" or "Wp" (watts-peak). Real-world output is typically 60-80% of peak due to non-ideal conditions. Example: 100 Wp panel produces ~60-80W in typical outdoor conditions.

area.description: Total panel area. Unit: "m2" or "cm2". Used with efficiency to cross-check peak-power: peak_power = area x 1000W/m2 x efficiency. Also used for physical packaging constraints on the robot body.

efficiency.description: Solar cell conversion efficiency as a fraction (0-1). The ratio of electrical power output to incident solar power. Monocrystalline: 0.20-0.24. Polycrystalline: 0.15-0.20. Thin-film: 0.10-0.15. GaAs: 0.28-0.30.

voltage-mpp.description: Voltage at Maximum Power Point (Vmpp) under STC. Unit: "V". The MPPT charge controller operates the panel at this voltage to extract maximum power. Example: 18V for a nominal 12V panel, 36V for a nominal 24V panel.

current-mpp.description: Current at Maximum Power Point (Impp) under STC. Unit: "A". peak-power = voltage-mpp x current-mpp.

open-circuit-voltage.description: Open-circuit voltage (Voc) under STC. Unit: "V". The maximum voltage the panel produces with no load. Always higher than voltage-mpp. Used for charge controller input voltage rating.

mppt.description: Whether the associated charge controller uses Maximum Power Point Tracking. true = MPPT controller (extracts 15-30% more energy than PWM in varying conditions). false = PWM or direct connection. An agent factors this into energy harvest estimates.

solar_source.description: Solar panel energy source: converts sunlight to electricity via photovoltaic cells. Used on agricultural robots, exploration rovers, long-endurance UAS, outdoor monitoring platforms, and space systems. Solar provides continuous power during daylight but output varies with irradiance, temperature, panel orientation, and shading. An agent combines solar peak-power with battery capacity to estimate sustained runtime: during daylight the panel charges the battery and powers the system, at night the battery alone provides power.

sphere.description: Sphere geometry primitive centered at the parent pose origin.

name.description: Name of the sub-part (submesh/node) within the mesh file to load. SDF mesh/submesh/name. Required.

center.description: If true, recenter the selected submesh so its geometric center is at the mesh origin. SDF mesh/submesh/center. Default: false.

submesh.description: Selects a single named sub-part (a node/group) inside a multi-part mesh file, so only that piece is loaded. Maps to SDF mesh/submesh (name + center). Use when a CAD export packs several bodies into one file and this geometry is just one of them.

capacitance.description: Total capacitance. Unit: "F" (farads). Supercapacitors typically range from 1F to 3000F per cell. Series/parallel configurations adjust the effective capacitance and voltage. Energy stored = 0.5 x C x V^2.

max-voltage.description: Maximum rated voltage. Unit: "V". Individual cells are typically 2.5-2.7V; series stacks reach 12V, 24V, 48V or higher. Exceeding max voltage causes gas generation and permanent damage.

esr.description: Equivalent Series Resistance. Unit: "mohm" (milliohms). Determines power loss during charge/discharge and maximum current capability: I_max approx V / ESR. Lower ESR = higher power capability. Typical: 0.3-50 mohm depending on size.

max-current.description: Maximum continuous discharge current. Unit: "A". Supercapacitors can deliver very high currents (hundreds of amps) for short durations. Limited by ESR heating.

peak-current.description: Peak (burst) current for short pulses. Unit: "A". Can be significantly higher than max-current for pulses under 1 second.

energy.description: Total stored energy at max voltage. Unit: "Wh" or "J". Computed from 0.5 x C x V^2 but useful to state explicitly. Much less than batteries of similar volume: a 3000F/2.7V cell stores ~3 Wh vs ~50 Wh for a similar-sized Li-ion cell.

cells-series.description: Number of cells in series. Determines pack voltage: max-voltage = cells x cell-voltage. Requires balancing circuitry.

cycle-life.description: Rated cycle life: number of charge/discharge cycles to 80% capacitance retention. Supercapacitors typically last 500,000 to 1,000,000+ cycles, far exceeding batteries.

supercapacitor_source.description: Supercapacitor (ultracapacitor) energy source: stores energy electrostatically rather than chemically. Compared to batteries: much higher power density (fast charge/discharge in seconds), much lower energy density (stores less total energy), and near-unlimited cycle life (millions of cycles vs hundreds for batteries). Used for peak power buffering (absorbs regenerative braking energy, provides burst current for motor acceleration), bridge power during battery hot-swap, and smoothing pulsed loads. An agent combines supercapacitor burst capability with battery sustained power for complete power budget analysis.

restitution.description: Coefficient of restitution (bounciness). 0 = perfectly inelastic (no bounce), 1 = perfectly elastic (full bounce). Dimensionless, range [0, 1].

contact.description: Contact dynamics parameters (stiffness, damping) for physics simulation.

surface.description: Inline contact physics for a collision shape: friction, restitution (bounciness), and contact dynamics used by physics simulators. Appears only under <collision>. Inline-only (no named contact-material library) -- matching URDF (per-link <gazebo> mu/kp) and SDF (per-collision <surface>), neither of which has a reusable contact handle. Not to be confused with <dynamic-surface> (functional aero/wheel/gripper surfaces on a comp).

swing1.description: Cone half-angle about local Z, in radians. The maximum swing away from the twist axis in the first perpendicular direction. Required when <swing_limit> is present.

swing2.description: Cone half-angle about local Y, in radians. Omit for a circular cone (defaults to swing1); set different from swing1 for an elliptic cone.

effort.description: Maximum swing effort (torque, Nm) resisting motion into the cone limit. Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).

velocity.description: Maximum swing angular velocity (rad/s). Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).

swing_limit.description: Swing-cone limit for a ball (spherical) joint's two SWING degrees of freedom (the twist DOF is bounded separately by <twist_limit>). Half-angles in radians about the two axes perpendicular to the twist axis (local X). swing1 == swing2 (or swing2 omitted) => a CIRCULAR cone; swing1 != swing2 => an ELLIPTIC cone. This maps 1:1 to Bullet btConeTwistConstraint::setLimit(swing1, swing2, twist), USD UsdPhysicsSphericalJoint (circular/elliptic cone), and MuJoCo's scalar cone (set swing1=swing2, omit twist). Optional; an omitted <swing_limit> means the swing is unbounded (ODE-compatible free ball). Only valid on type="ball".

pose.description: Pose of the sensor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

driver.description: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.

noise.description: Noise model for the sensor output.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).

rows.description: Number of rows in the taxel array. Defines the spatial layout along one axis of the sensing surface. Example: 4 rows x 4 cols = 16 taxels in a fingertip pad.

cols.description: Number of columns in the taxel array. Together with rows, defines the rectangular grid of sensing elements.

taxels.description: Total number of individual tactile sensing elements (taxels). For regular grids, taxels = rows x cols. For irregular layouts (e.g., curved fingertip, hexagonal packing), specify taxels directly when rows/cols do not apply. Example: 160 taxels on a SynTouch BioTac, 32 on a XELA uSkin patch.

spatial-resolution.description: Center-to-center spacing between adjacent taxels. Unit: "mm". Determines the minimum feature size the sensor can resolve through touch. Example: 2.5 mm for a fingertip array, 10 mm for a body-skin patch. Smaller spacing = finer spatial detail but more wiring and processing.

pressure-range.description: Measurable contact pressure range per taxel. Unit: "kPa" or "N". min = minimum detectable pressure (sensitivity threshold), max = saturation pressure. Example: min="0.1" max="100" unit="kPa" for a capacitive fingertip. Light touch is ~1 kPa, firm grip is 10-50 kPa, maximum grip can exceed 100 kPa.

sensing-area.description: Total active sensing area of the tactile surface. Unit: "mm2" or "cm2". Example: 314 mm2 for a circular fingertip pad (20mm diameter), 2500 mm2 for a 50x50 palm patch.

type.description: Tactile sensor technology type (capacitive, resistive, piezoelectric, barometric, optical). Required. Determines the sensing principle and typical characteristics: capacitive and barometric are best for static pressure, piezoelectric for dynamic events (slip, texture), optical for rich 3D contact geometry.

tactile_sensor.description: Tactile sensor for distributed contact/pressure measurement across a surface. Unlike force sensors (single-point measurement), tactile sensors provide spatially distributed pressure data across an array of sensing elements (taxels). Used on robot fingertips, palms, grippers, and body skin for grasp planning, slip detection, object recognition by touch, and safe physical interaction. Extends sensor_base with tactile-specific parameters: array dimensions, taxel count, spatial resolution, and pressure range.

fuel.description: Fuel type: "gasoline", "diesel", "hydrogen", "compressed-air", "nitrogen", "propane", "ethanol", "jet-a". Determines energy density and handling requirements.

pressure.description: Storage pressure (for compressed gases). Unit: "bar" or "psi". Example: 350 bar for hydrogen, 200 bar for compressed air.

flow.description: Flow characterization: how fluid exits the tank and at what rate. Defines delivery method (pressurized, regulated, pumped, gravity), outlet pressure, max/peak flow rates, and regulation mechanism. Without this, the tank is just a capacity number with no delivery information.

tank_source.description: Fuel/gas tank energy source. For combustion engines, hydrogen fuel cells, compressed air systems, or pneumatic actuators. Defines fuel type, volume, pressure, energy content, and flow characterization (how fluid exits and at what rate). An agent needs both capacity (how much energy is stored) and flow (how fast it can be delivered) to compute runtime and power capability.

pose.description: Pose of the sensor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).

driver.description: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.

noise.description: Noise model for the sensor output.

data-output.description: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).

type.description: Temperature sensor type: thermistor (NTC/PTC, common in motors), rtd (PT100/PT1000, high accuracy), thermocouple (K/J/T type, wide range), ir (non-contact infrared). Required.

temperature_sensor.description: Temperature sensor: thermistor, RTD, thermocouple, or IR. Common use: motor winding temperature monitoring (NTC thermistor in motor signal connector), ambient temperature, battery cell temperature. Extends sensor_base with temperature sensor type attribute.

ground-pressure.description: Ground pressure (vehicle weight / total track contact area). Unit: "kPa". Lower = better soft terrain performance.

track_surface.description: Tracked vehicle surface (tank treads, rubber tracks). Defines the track geometry and ground contact properties. Used for high-traction vehicles on rough terrain.

items.description: Motor endpoint(s) driving this transmission, slash-path "comp_name/motor_name" (or a bare motor name when document-unique). A simple reduction has ONE motor; a differential coupling has TWO motor endpoints (use role="input" to disambiguate which motor drives which output).

motor.description: Motor endpoint(s) driving this transmission, slash-path "comp_name/motor_name" (or a bare motor name when document-unique). A simple reduction has ONE motor; a differential coupling has TWO motor endpoints (use role="input" to disambiguate which motor drives which output).

items.description: Joint endpoint(s) this transmission drives, by joint name. A simple reduction has ONE joint; a gearbox couples TWO joint endpoints (role="reference" plus role="driven") geared by the reduction ratio; a differential has TWO joint outputs (role="output").

joint.description: Joint endpoint(s) this transmission drives, by joint name. A simple reduction has ONE joint; a gearbox couples TWO joint endpoints (role="reference" plus role="driven") geared by the reduction ratio; a differential has TWO joint outputs (role="output").

reduction.description: Gear reduction ratio (motor_speed / joint_speed). Values greater than 1 indicate speed reduction / torque multiplication. For example, 100 means the motor turns 100 times for each joint revolution.

efficiency.description: Mechanical efficiency of the transmission as a fraction in [0, 1]. 1.0 = lossless, 0.9 = 90% efficient. Accounts for friction losses in gears, belts, and bearings.

backlash.description: Mechanical backlash (dead zone) at the joint output. Unit: typically "rad" for rotary or "m" for linear transmissions.

items.description: Compliant spring element(s) in the drivetrain. Zero springs = rigid actuator. One series spring = SEA. One parallel spring = PEA. One of each = SEA+PEA combination. Springs with clutch/equilibrium-actuator/stiffness-actuator attributes express CPEA, AE-PEA, and VSA architectures respectively.

spring.description: Compliant spring element(s) in the drivetrain. Zero springs = rigid actuator. One series spring = SEA. One parallel spring = PEA. One of each = SEA+PEA combination. Springs with clutch/equilibrium-actuator/stiffness-actuator attributes express CPEA, AE-PEA, and VSA architectures respectively.

name.description: Unique name for this transmission (e.g., "shoulder_trans", "wheel_fl_belt"). Required.

type.description: Mechanical transmission type (simple, differential, belt, gear, planetary, cycloidal, harmonic, strain-wave, worm). Optional; defaults to simple if not specified.

encoder.description: Name reference to a joint-side encoder sensor. This is the encoder on the output side of the transmission (after the gearbox), providing higher-accuracy joint position feedback than the motor-side encoder. Optional: not all transmissions have output encoders.

visual.description: Name of the visual element containing this transmission's mesh for 3D highlighting.

mesh.description: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this transmission.

transmission.description: Mechanical power transmission connecting motor(s) to joint(s). Defines the gear reduction ratio, efficiency, backlash, and optional compliant elements (springs) for the mechanical coupling between motor output and joint input. A single motor + single joint endpoint is a SIMPLE reduction (the common case). MULTIPLE endpoints express a coupling: a GEARBOX gears two joint endpoints by the reduction ratio (a reference joint and a driven joint, distinguished by the endpoint role attribute); a DIFFERENTIAL couples two motor endpoints to two joint endpoints (role input/output). A transmission without spring elements is a rigid actuator. Adding a series spring creates a Series Elastic Actuator (SEA). Adding a parallel spring creates a Parallel Elastic Actuator (PEA). Both can be combined. Advanced variants (CPEA, AE-PEA, VSA) are expressed through spring attributes (clutch, equilibrium-actuator, stiffness-actuator).

ref.description: Slash-path reference to the motor or joint (e.g., "shoulder_comp/shoulder_motor", or the bare "shoulder_joint" when it is document-unique). The last '/'-separated segment is the leaf (motor or joint name); everything before it names the component; leaf names contain no separator. Slash is the only accepted separator: a dot is not a reference separator. Required.

role.description: Optional role of this endpoint within a multi-endpoint coupling: reference/driven for a gearbox (which joint is the geared reference and which is driven), input/output for a differential (which motors are inputs and which joints are outputs). Omit for a simple single-motor/single-joint reduction, where the endpoint's role is unambiguous.

transmission_endpoint.description: Reference to a motor or joint endpoint in a transmission. Uses a slash-path "comp/motor" (or "comp/joint") to identify the target across components: the last '/'-separated segment is the leaf (the motor or joint name), everything before it names the component, and a bare leaf name is legal iff it is document-unique. Slash is the ONLY reference separator: a dot is not a separator. In a multi-endpoint coupling (gearbox, differential) the optional role attribute disambiguates this endpoint's part in the coupling. Endpoint resolution is deferred to the companion validator.

stiffness.description: Spring stiffness (rate). Unit: "Nm/rad" for rotary, "N/m" for linear. For fixed-stiffness springs (SEA, PEA, CPEA, AE-PEA): specify the text content as the single stiffness value. For variable-stiffness actuators (VSA): use min and max attributes for the adjustable range. Example: 4.5 Nm/rad for HEBI X8-9 SEA, or min="5" max="500" unit="Nm/rad" for a VSA. This is the defining parameter of a compliant actuator: it determines force control bandwidth, impact energy absorption, and torque measurement resolution (torque = stiffness x deflection).

max-deflection.description: Maximum spring deflection before mechanical hard stop. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. Defines the torque saturation limit: max_torque = stiffness x max_deflection. Beyond this deflection the actuator behaves rigidly. Example: 0.15 rad for a typical SEA torsion spring. Also determines maximum stored elastic energy: E = 0.5 x stiffness x max_deflection^2.

damping.description: Viscous damping in the spring element. Unit: "Nm.s/rad" for rotary, "N.s/m" for linear. Most springs have minimal inherent damping; this captures any intentional damping added to the compliant element. Affects oscillation settling time and force control stability.

equilibrium.description: Fixed spring rest position (equilibrium point) for PEA configurations. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. The joint angle at which the parallel spring exerts zero force. Typically tuned to the most common operating posture for optimal gravity compensation. For AE-PEA (adjustable equilibrium), use equilibrium-range instead.

equilibrium-range.description: Adjustable equilibrium range for AE-PEA configurations. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. min and max define the range over which the equilibrium motor can shift the spring rest position. The equilibrium-actuator attribute identifies the motor that performs this adjustment. Example: min="-1.57" max="0.0" for a knee joint that needs gravity compensation anywhere from full flexion to standing.

clutch-power.description: Electrical power required to operate the clutch mechanism for CPEA configurations. Unit: "W". For electromagnetic clutches: power to hold engaged (typically 1-5W). For mechanical latches: power for the actuation pulse only (zero holding power). Only applicable when the clutch attribute is set.

engage-time.description: Clutch engagement/disengagement latency for CPEA configurations. Unit: "ms". Time from command to full engagement. Electromagnetic clutches: 2-10 ms. Mechanical latches: 10-50 ms. Affects how quickly the system can switch between compliant and rigid behavior (e.g., switching between stance and swing phase in walking).

placement.description: Where the spring sits in the drivetrain relative to the gearbox and motor. "series": between gearbox output and joint output (SEA): the spring deflects under load, enabling force sensing via dual-encoder deflection measurement and providing inherent compliance. "parallel": alongside the motor, between a fixed anchor and the joint output (PEA): the spring provides a passive torque that assists or opposes the motor, typically tuned for gravity compensation. Required.

type.description: Physical spring construction: "torsion-bar" (solid or tubular bar that twists, compact, common in SEAs), "leaf" (flat spring that bends, easy to manufacture), "coil" (helical compression/extension spring, common in linear actuators), "cable-linear" (cable-driven with linear spring in tension), "gas" (gas spring, provides near-constant force over stroke), "custom" (application-specific design). Optional.

torque-sensing.description: How joint torque is measured using this spring. "spring-deflection": torque derived from the angular difference between motor-side and output-side encoders multiplied by spring stiffness (torque = k x delta_theta): the standard SEA approach, requires two encoders. "strain-gauge": dedicated strain gauge or load cell on the spring element (e.g., Franka Panda joint torque sensors). "current": torque estimated from motor current (torque = Kt x I): less accurate, no spring needed but listed here for completeness. "none": no torque sensing. Optional; only applicable for series springs.

clutch.description: Clutch mechanism for engaging/disengaging a parallel spring (CPEA). "electromagnetic": fast switching (2-10 ms), requires continuous power to hold engaged. "mechanical-latch": zero holding power, slower switching (10-50 ms), uses a bistable mechanism. "one-way": ratchet or sprag clutch that locks in one direction and freewheels in the other. "none" or omit: no clutch, spring is permanently engaged. Only applicable for parallel springs.

equilibrium-actuator.description: Reference to a motor (slash-path "comp/motor", or a bare motor name when document-unique) that adjusts the spring equilibrium position for AE-PEA configurations. This second motor is typically small and slow: it only moves when the operating posture changes, shifting where the parallel spring exerts zero force for optimal gravity compensation at any joint angle. Only applicable for parallel springs with equilibrium-range.

stiffness-actuator.description: Reference to a motor (slash-path "comp/motor", or a bare motor name when document-unique) that adjusts spring stiffness at runtime for Variable Stiffness Actuator (VSA) configurations. The second motor changes the effective lever arm or preload on the spring, varying stiffness between the min and max values specified in the stiffness element. Only applicable for series springs with variable stiffness range.

transmission_spring.description: Compliant element (spring) in a transmission drivetrain. The presence of a spring element is what distinguishes compliant actuators from rigid ones. A spring in series between the gearbox and the joint output creates a Series Elastic Actuator (SEA): enabling torque sensing via deflection measurement, impact absorption, backdrivability through high-ratio gearboxes, and inherent safety for human interaction. A spring in parallel with the motor creates a Parallel Elastic Actuator (PEA): providing passive gravity compensation to reduce motor effort. Multiple spring elements are allowed: an SEA+PEA combination uses one series spring for force sensing and one parallel spring for gravity compensation. Advanced variants add a clutch (CPEA, clutchable PEA, engages/disengages the parallel spring on demand), an equilibrium motor (AE-PEA, adjustable equilibrium PEA, shifts the spring rest position at runtime), or a stiffness motor (VSA, variable stiffness actuator, changes spring stiffness at runtime via a second motor).

link-type.description: The URDF link/@type (an undocumented PR2-era attribute). Preserved verbatim for URDF round-trip; no HCDF semantics.

urdf_compat_comp.description: Container for URDF-only, zero-CPS fields on a component, kept out of the clean core. Optional; omit for native HCDF authoring.

safety_controller.description: URDF safety_controller, preserved for round-trip. Only meaningful on joints that map to URDF revolute/prismatic.

urdf_compat_joint.description: Container for URDF-only, zero-CPS fields on a joint, kept out of the clean core. Optional; omit for native HCDF authoring.

pose.description: Pose of the visual relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians). Default: identity (no offset).

name.description: Unique name for this visual within the component. Required. Used for programmatic toggling and identification.

toggle.description: Toggle group name. Visuals sharing the same toggle group can be shown/hidden together at runtime (e.g., "leds", "covers").

name-origin.description: Provenance of the name (authored vs converter-synthesized). Optional; absence means authored. A converter importing URDF (whose visuals have no name) sets this to "synthesized" so the name can be stripped on URDF export.

visual.description: Visual representation of a component for rendering. Contains either a high-fidelity 3D model reference or a geometry primitive fallback (or both, where model is preferred and geometry is the fallback). Multiple visuals per component are allowed for multi-part rendering.

visual_geometry.description: Visual geometry: primitive shapes ONLY (box, cylinder, sphere, capsule, cone, ellipsoid). There is deliberately NO <mesh> here -- a *visual* mesh is the self-contained GLB/glTF <model> (the rich-appearance arm of <visual>), never a bare geometry mesh. So "a visual mesh is GLB-only" is enforced by the grammar itself. Frustum is excluded (sensor-FOV only). Used in <visual>'s flat/primitive arm with an optional flat <color>.

type.description: Wheel type: "driven" (has motor), "steering" (steerable), "caster" (passive swivel), "omni" (omnidirectional rollers), "mecanum" (45-degree rollers). Optional.

wheel_surface.description: Wheel ground contact surface. Defines the tire/wheel geometry and friction properties for ground vehicles. The motor driving this wheel is defined separately; the wheel surface describes the contact interface with the ground.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this HCDF file describes. For a top-level robot: the robot's purpose and key characteristics (e.g., "CogniPilot humanoid mobile base research platform with dual 7-DOF arms and TSN backbone"). For a reusable sub-assembly: the module's function and interface (e.g., "7-DOF manipulator arm with HEBI X8-series SEA actuators, 802.3dm daisy-chain, and force/torque sensing at wrist"). Helps humans and AI agents understand the file's contents without parsing the full document.

author.description: Author or organization that created this HCDF file (e.g., "CogniPilot Foundation", "HEBI Robotics", "Jane Doe"). For composed systems, each included file retains its own author, allowing BOM tools to trace which vendor or team provided each sub-assembly. Optional.

license.description: License governing use of this HCDF file and the design it describes. Use SPDX license identifiers when possible (e.g., "Apache-2.0", "BSD-3-Clause", "MIT", "CERN-OHL-S-2.0" for open hardware, "LicenseRef-Proprietary" for closed designs). For composed systems, each included file can carry a different license, enabling mixed open-source and proprietary sub-assemblies. Optional.

url.description: Canonical URL for this HCDF file's project, documentation, or source repository (e.g., "https://github.com/CogniPilot/hcdformat"). Provides a stable reference for humans and tooling to find updates, issues, and related resources. Optional.

items.description: Component definitions (rigid bodies / hardware assemblies).
Kinematic joint connections between components.
Named joint groups for planning and control (e.g., left_arm, locomotion).

group.description: Named joint groups for planning and control (e.g., left_arm, locomotion).

items.description: Named kinematic states / poses (e.g., home, transport).

state.description: Named kinematic states / poses (e.g., home, transport).

self-collision-disable.description: Component pairs to skip for self-collision checking.

color.description: Reusable document-level color definitions (each @name + @rgba), referenced by name from visual <color> elements. HCDF's flat-appearance palette; replaces the former bundled <material> -- rich appearance is baked into the GLB <model>, and contact physics lives on <collision><surface>.

items.description: External HCDF file includes for model composition.

include.description: External HCDF file includes for model composition.

items.description: Document-level vendor/domain-specific extension data. Used (among other things) as the lax home for model-level (reference-less) URDF <gazebo> blocks and for top-level non-URDF-schema elements quarantined on import (e.g. <ros2_control> under domain "org.ros2.control"), preserving them byte-faithfully for round-trip without polluting the typed core.

extension.description: Document-level vendor/domain-specific extension data. Used (among other things) as the lax home for model-level (reference-less) URDF <gazebo> blocks and for top-level non-URDF-schema elements quarantined on import (e.g. <ros2_control> under domain "org.ros2.control"), preserving them byte-faithfully for round-trip without polluting the typed core.

name.description: Name of the robot, platform, or sub-assembly described by this file. Required. For top-level robot descriptions, this is the robot's model name (e.g., "cogni-humanoid-v2", "quadrotor-x500"). For reusable sub-assemblies, this is the module name (e.g., "7dof-arm", "stereo-head-v2", "hebi-x8-9"). When a file is imported via include, the include's name attribute provides the instance name (e.g., "left_arm"), while this attribute provides the module identity. Use lowercase-with-hyphens by convention.

version.description: HCDF schema version this file conforms to. Current: 1.0. Pattern-validated MAJOR.MINOR. Core XSD validation is ordered and closed: unknown core elements are rejected, and domain-specific content belongs inside <extension>. Typed-loader compatibility is defined by the loader's version policy. Tooling binds to the embedded canonical hcdf.xsd by content SHA-256, not by this string alone.

body-frame.description: Body-frame axis convention for all pose values in this file. FLU (X-forward, Y-left, Z-up): common in ground robotics and humanoid platforms. FRD (X-forward, Y-right, Z-down): common in aerospace and flight controllers. All xyz and rpy values in this document are expressed in the specified body-frame convention. Optional; when omitted, consumers should not assume a default and must either infer from context or require explicit specification. Semantic rule: all files in an include chain must use the same body-frame.

world-frame.description: World-frame (navigation/map frame) axis convention for global coordinates. ENU (X-east, Y-north, Z-up): common in GIS, surveying, and ground robotics. NED (X-north, Y-east, Z-down): common in aerospace, marine navigation, and flight controllers. Determines how global poses, waypoints, and map-relative coordinates are interpreted. Independent of body-frame. Optional; when omitted, consumers should not assume a default. Semantic rule: all files in an include chain must use the same world-frame.
